question: Why could Bach's Mass in B minor not be heard complete in any church service of his time?
answer: It was too long for any liturgy. Lutheran Leipzig used only a short Latin Mass, a Kyrie and Gloria; Bach wrote those two parts in 1733 for the Catholic court at Dresden, seeking a court title. He added the rest in 1748 and 1749, largely from older music. The first recorded complete performance came in 1859.
move: A work can be finished long before any occasion exists for it.
source: Stauffer, Bach: The Mass in B Minor
reference: Stauffer, Bach: The Mass in B Minor: The Great Catholic Mass, Yale University Press, 2003
